messages:
mike: hi all, new to the infra team — trying to get my first CI run green. GitHub Actions job 'build-and-publish' fails on the push to ghcr.io with 401/403. unsure if this is a perms issue or my secrets are misnamed.
trina: welcome mike! :wave: do you have a repo secret for the registry? we usually name it `GHCR_TOKEN` for Actions, and `GHCR_PAT` for Buildkite.
mike: i added a secret called `REGISTRY_TOKEN` because i thought generic names were easier. logs show: 
```
error: failed to push to registry: unauthorized: access to the requested resource is not authorized
```
so probably a name mismatch?
grant: name mismatch could be it if the workflow expects a specific env. which workflow file are you using? can you paste the `uses` steps around `docker/build-push-action`?
mike: here's the relevant snippet from .github/workflows/publish.yml: 
```
- name: Log in to GHCR
  uses: docker/login-action@v2
  with:
    registry: ghcr.io
    username: ${{ github.actor }}
    password: ${{ secrets.GHCR_TOKEN }}
```

mike: so i should rename my secret to GHCR_TOKEN?
trina: yep. also note org SSO can require you to use org-approved apps/tokens. if the token is from a user who hasn't authorized SSO, pushes will fail even with a valid PAT.
devops-bot: Workflow run 88 failed (publish job) — see https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/actions/runs/88 for details.
grant: two routes: 1) create a repo-scoped personal access token from a user in the `ci-deployers` team (ensure packages:write) and add it as GHCR_TOKEN, or 2) we create a machine/service account token (preferred). i can create `redwood-ghcr-bot` and grant package write on the repo.
mike: would be nice to avoid tying it to my personal account. thanks.
trina: @grant can you add mike to the onboarding checklist and rotate creds later? also mike — after we add the machine user you'll need no extra GitHub install access.
grants: will do (typo: i meant grant).
grant: created machine user `redwood-ghcr-bot`, gave packages:write for repo, generated PAT, added it as `GHCR_TOKEN` in repo secrets (masked). installed docker login action permission.
devops-bot: Workflow re-run started: run 89 (branch: onboarding/mike-first-build).
mike: build 89 ✅ passed. super helpful. quick questions: where's the short note on naming conventions for CI secrets? and who owns rotating the machine token?
trina: naming doc is at `docs/dev/ci-secrets.md` — open a PR if anything is missing. we schedule token rotations quarterly; ops/sre owns rotation but tag @grant in infra for repo-specific updates.
mike: got it, thanks everyone! :tada:
